problem: Learning-based ObjectNav methods (end-to-end RL, map-based, black-box region classifiers) are opaque and computationally heavy, and rarely exploit explicit object-region co-occurrence and region adjacency priors to decide which region to explore next.
motivation: Humans search for objects using commonsense priors, e.g. a sink is likely in a kitchen and an oven suggests a kitchen. The paper encodes these priors as a probabilistic Spatial Relational Graph learned from trajectories in MP3D scenes. It then embeds that graph with a GCN to rank visible regions, aiming for an interpretable and cheap alternative to deep region classifiers.
key_idea: Learn a Spatial Relational Graph of region-region adjacency and object-region co-occurrence, embed it with a GCN trained on valid trajectories, and at test time use Bayesian inference over the SRG to estimate visible regions and pick the one whose embedding is most similar to the target object.
insight: Ablating the SRG/trajectory-trained GCN scoring (replaced by choosing a random visible object) sharply drops success, e.g. bed 0.60 vs 0.9983, picture 0.395 vs 0.95, which shows the learned priors carry the performance. Replacing the region classification network (RCN) with SRG-based Bayesian estimation costs only a little success (0.773 vs 0.751) while being incremental, cheaper and interpretable. Caveats: object recognition, region labels and the map are assumed ground truth, so results reflect the quality of the priors under near-oracle perception.
method: Valid trajectory generation: in known MP3D scenes, the agent uses a shortest path follower to the nearest instance of each target class and records the sequence of regions traversed (18,488 trajectories).

Spatial Relational Graph: nodes are object and region categories (19 objects, 28 regions, 47 nodes, 104 edges); 'includes' edges are weighted by object-region co-occurrence frequency, and adjacency edges by co-occurrence divided by the minimum region frequency, built from 59 MP3D scenes.

GCN embedding: a 3-layer GCNConv over the SRG (edges with weight <=0.5 pruned) with one-hot node features and 128-d output, trained with sigmoid cross-entropy. It pulls together regions on valid prefix paths and the target, and pushes apart nodes of synthetic invalid prefix paths.

Visible region estimation: naive-Bayes inference p(R|o_1..o_k) proportional to the product of p(o|R) from the SRG, with a uniform prior. Each visible object is combined with its k nearest visible objects, and the argmax region label is assigned.
Region selection: choose the visible region whose GCN embedding has the highest cosine similarity to the target object's embedding.

Action controller: an off-the-shelf shortest path follower / planner moves to the chosen region and then to the target when it is seen. Success is within 1 m, with a 350-step budget, 0.3 m moves and 30° turns.

setting.backbone: 3-layer GCN (GCNConv, 128-d embeddings) trained from scratch plus SRG Bayesian inference; off-the-shelf shortest-path planner
setting.training_data: 18,488 valid trajectories from 12 MP3D scenes for the GCN; SRG statistics from 59 MP3D scenes (a further count of 51 scenes is also mentioned)
setting.observation: egocentric view with ground-truth object recognition and region labels; the agent is assumed to know the entire map, objects and regions
setting.action_space: low-level Habitat actions (forward 0.3 m, turn 30°, look up/down, stop) via a shortest-path follower to region goals
setting.privileged: Perfect object recognition; region-labelled semantic annotations and map knowledge; shortest path follower with geodesic information used for local navigation

numbers.eval_set_note: 5 MP3D scenes (17DRP5sb8fy, rPc6DW4iMge, S9hNv5qa7GM, b8cTxDM8gDG, EDJbREhghzL) with 250 episodes each; paper text also mentions 6 scenes / 1500 episodes
numbers.backbone: SRG Bayesian region estimation + GCN embeddings
numbers.extra: ground-truth object recognition; agent assumed to know map/regions; 350-step budget; success radius 1.0 m
ground-truth object recognition; more computationally expensive than SRG

numbers_note: Metrics are printed as fractions (0.751 = 75.1%). The appendix table for 6 scenes and 19 objects shows an average success of 94.133% and SPL 0.658, but its setup differs and it is not in the main tables. Baseline comparison (Table 1) gives only Success; the ANS, ANS+GCExp and Random numbers are the baselines' own. Scene counts are inconsistent in the text (5 vs 6 scenes).
results: With SRG region estimation the framework reaches Success 0.751, SPL 0.530, SoftSPL 0.553 and DTS 2.348 m, versus ANS 0.69, ANS+GCExp 0.72 and Random 0.0056. The RCN variant is slightly better (0.773) but far more computationally expensive. Ablating the trained spatial-relation scoring reduces per-object success, e.g. bed 0.60 to 0.9983.
limitations: Assumes perfect object recognition, region labels and knowledge of the map/regions, so results are optimistic and do not reflect real perception noise.
Evaluated only on a few MP3D scenes in simulation with no real-robot trials; scene counts are inconsistently reported, and baselines are compared using only Success.
Bayesian estimation relies on an object-independence assumption and a fixed 19-object / 28-region vocabulary.
